newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Moroccan bourse returns to stable trend.
newsitem.headline: Moroccan bourse returns to stable trend.

text.p: The Casablanca stock market ended its two-hour session on Monday slightly higher, but stockbrokers said this was a return to a stable trend as expected by investors.
The bourse all-share index rose to 431.14, up 0.10 percent on last week's session.

"Despite the index slight rise, the market remained stable as some listed stocks started publishing their half-year results which were in line with market expectation," a stockbroker at Upline Securities said.
The leading Ciments de l'Oriental and several other cement companies published postive results in September as expected by market investors, he added.
CIOR remained unchanged at 355 dirhams, while les Ciments de Meknes rose 34 dirhams to 500 dirhams. Les Ciments du Maroc, rose one dirham to 366 dirhams.
Societe Nationale d'Investissement, which has interests in a group of cement firms, remained stable at 600 dirhams on the previous week.
Banque Commerciale du Maroc traded at 700 dirhams with no change on the previous session.
The significant gain was made by ONA Group which closed at 450 dirhams, up five dirhams on Friday session.
An estimated 30,000 shares of ONA exchanged hands on Monday, traders said.
Samir refinery, Morocco's main oil plant and in which the government expects to sell up to 51 perecent stake to foreign oil investors by end 1996, lost one dirham to close at 250 dirhams.
The bourse volume was 24.9 million dirhams, up from 23.8 million dirhams last Friday. ($1= 8.7 dirhams)
